sessions.title: Session A
learning_outcomes: Track objects from left to right with their eyes and with a Finger.
Recognize details in shapes and objects as being similar or different from each other.
Tell a story using pictures.
Follow lines with a finger.

activities.title: Make Comparisons
activities.content:
Compare illustrations
• Show pupils how to open their Pupil Books 
to the first page. Hold up the pupils Book so 
that pupils can see the page for lesson 1 and 
point to the first illustration.
• Say: Ali ali bulukondiŋo loo nataali foloo koto, komeŋ teŋ. Ñiŋ mu daafeŋ jumaa le 
ti? Haa ninsoo le mu.
• Point to the next picture in the row, to the right of the bull.
• Say: Ali ŋà ¥ bulukondiŋo loo nataali foloo kaŋ. Fo a niŋ nataali fulanjaŋo mu kiliŋ 
ne ti baŋ? Hanii!
• Point to the next picture in the row. 
• Say: "Ali ŋà ñiŋ doo fanaŋ juubee. A niŋ nataali foloo mulunta le baŋ? Hanii!"
• Point to the final picture in the row. 
• Say: Fo ñiŋ niŋ nataali foloo mulunta le baŋ? Haa. 
• Continue this process with the other rows, each time asking the pupils to study the 
first illustration and find the other illustration in the row that matches. 
Compare shapes
• Ask pupils to turn to the next page in the Pupil Book.
• Use the same process as the activity above with the shapes on the next page of the 
Pupil Book.

activities.title: Story sequence
activities.content:
Tell a story using pictures
• Show the next page in the Pupil Book.
• Say: Ali ali bulukondiŋo loo nataali foloo koto. Moo ñiŋ be, munne ke kaŋ?

• Call on two pupils to respond.
• Talk with pupils about each picture in the sequence (1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6). Ask pupils 
what  people are doing in each picture and ask questions to help them think about 
the pictures.
• Ask pupils to look at the pictures and describe the story the pictures are telling. 
Help them see that the woman is preparing "banku".

activities.title: Trace lines
activities.content:
Follow lines with a finger
• Show the next page in the Pupil Book.
• Say: Kambaanoo meŋ be nataaloo kono, a be munne la? Ali ŋà a maakoyi a ye 
katoo damfu poosoo kono! Ali pareeta le baŋ? Ali bulukondiŋo coodi katoo be faŋ 
na meŋ naa.
• Show pupils how to trace the line from the ball to the goal with a finger.
• Say: Suloo be munne ke kaŋ? ali ye a miira, a lafita munne la? 
• Watch as pupils trace the line from the monkey to the banana with a finger.
• Repeat with the remaining image.

sessions.title: Session B
learning_outcomes: Recognize the front cover, and title of a book.
Apply new words learned to own life and use new words in conversation.
Use background knowledge to build meaning.
Use verbal and nonverbal communication appropriately.

activities.title: Parts of a Book
activities.content:
Recognize the Grade parts of a book - cover, 
back, Title
•  Point to the cover and back of a book.
• Say: £ be karanna le, ka bo ñaato ka taa kooma Ñiŋ ne mu bukoo la ñaato kayito ti
• Say: Ñiŋ kumoolu mennu be kayito ñaato wolu le ka bukoo too fo Bukoo too le ka a 
fo ali ye, ¥ be naa meŋ karanna bukoo kono.
• Say: Niŋ ǹ futata taaliŋo labandulaa to ¥ be bukoo kooma je la le.

activities.title: Vocabulary – before reading
activities.content:
Teach and discuss vocabulary
• Tell pupils each word. Have them repeat it but do not write it on the board. Ask 
pupils what they know about each one.
• Discuss the word meaning, using gestures or illustrations to support 
understanding. If needed, help pupils understand the word by saying it in another 
language they know.. 
  tuuroo,   nandiŋ,   sanawu

activities.title: Read aloud
activities.content:
Read the following story aloud
• Use the appropriate big book or supplementary illustrations if available
• While reading, pause to think aloud and talk to pupils about the story at key 
moments such as when you come to a vocabulary word the pupils just learned.

Faatu dooyaa baata le!
Faatu mantara kontaaniriŋ nuŋ. A be suwo kono, a maŋ feŋ soto a be meŋ ke la. A ye 
a je ko a nandiŋ Binta be maanituwo le la.  
"N nandiŋ, naa ŋa i maakoyi." "Hanii Faatu, dookuwo diyaata i ye le baake!" Bituŋ a 
bota je, a taata.  A ye a je ko a sanawu be a la sinsiŋolu landi kuu kaŋ. "N kotoo, naa 
ŋa i maakoyi."
"Hanii Faatu, dookuwo diyaata i ye le baake!" Bituŋ a bota je, a taata. Wo koolaa le 
mu, a ye a kotookee je a be naakoo bindee kaŋ. "N kotoo, fo n si i maakoyi noo baŋ?"
"Hanii Faatu, dookuwo diyaata i ye le baake!" Bituŋ a bota je, a taata. Wo koolaa a 
ye a je ko a kotoo musoo be ala karambunto dookuwo le ke kaŋ. "N kotoo, naa n ŋe i 
maakoyi."
"Hanii Faatu, dookuwo diyaata i ye le baake!" Bituŋ a bota je, a taata. Wo koolaa 
a taata a faamaa yaa. A faamaa ye a ñininkaa, "N na moo Faatu, munne ye i niyo 
kuyaa?" 
Silaŋ n be munne ke la? Niŋ n ko n be maanoo tuu la, i ko dookuwo diyaata n ye le. 
Niŋ n ko n be sinsiŋolu landi kuu la, I ko dookuwo diyaata ye le.  Niŋ n ko n be naakoo 
bindee la, I ko dookuwo diyaata a ye le.  Niŋ n ko n be karambunto dookuwo ke la, I 
ko dookuwo diyaata a ye le. Silaŋ N be munne ke la? A faamaa ko, 
"Hee Faatu! i niyo kana kuyaa! I be meŋ kaŋ kuuke le. N suulata moo le ye n maakoyi, 
meŋ buloo koyita leemuna tembendoo la sinsiŋo kono. I be m maakoyi la le baŋ?"
A naata a maakoyi.

activities.title: Rapid review
activities.content:
Review the parts of a book - cover, back, title
• Call on a volunteer pupil to show the class which part of a book you start reading 
from. Ask what this part of the book it is called. (correct response: ("front page")
• Say: Ali ye taaliŋo too je mintoo le? (Answer: "Bukoo ñaato kayitoo)
• Call on a volunteer pupil to answer. Call on a second volunteer pupil to say the 
title of the story that was just read aloud.
• Say: Niŋ ¥ futata bukoo bandulaa to, ǹ ka munne je? (Answer: Bukoo bitindaŋ 
kayitoo)
• Call on a volunteer pupil to answer and point to the back of the book.

activities.title: Make Comparisons
activities.content:
Compare shapes of capital letters 
• Hold up the Pupil Book so that pupils can see 
the page and point to the first capital letter. 
Do not say the name of the letter - this is 
NOT an activity for pupils to learn letters. It 
is an activity for pupils to practice telling the 
difference between letter and shapes.
• Say: N be n bulukondiŋo coodi la kulu foloo la. Moo kanaa I buloo coodi. N be doo 
fanaŋ juubee la meŋ niŋ a ka muluŋyaa.
• Point to the next one in the row.
• Say: Ali ŋa n bulukondiŋo loo nataali foloo kaŋ. Fo a niŋ nataali fulanjaŋo mu kiliŋ 
ne ti baŋ? Hanii!
• Point to the next one in the row.
• Say: "Ali ŋà ñiŋ doo fanaŋ juubee. A niŋ nataali foloo mulunta le baŋ? Hanii!"
• Point to the final one in the row.
• Say: Fo ñiŋ niŋ foloo mu kiliŋ ne ti? Haa? 
• Continue this process with the other rows, each time asking the pupils to study the 
first capital letter and find the other one in the row that matches it.

Compare shapes
• Use the same process as the activity above with the small letters on the next page 
of the Pupil Book. Do not say the name of the letter - this is NOT an activity for 
pupils to learn letters. It is an activity for pupils to practice telling the difference 
between letter shapes.

activities.title: Describe differences
activities.content:
Talk about the differences between objects
• Hold up the Pupil Book so that pupils can see the four objects in the next activity. 
Ask pupils to point to the objects in their own books.
• Call on pupils to describe what images go together and why (there is no 1 correct 
answer)

activities.title: Trace lines
activities.content:
Follow lines with a finger
• Say: Ali ŋà bula ñiŋ tumboolu nooma! Foloo mu kerileŋo le ti! Ali ŋà ¥ bulukondiŋo 
laa a datidulaa to, ko a ka podi ñaameŋ kayitoo bala.
• Demonstrate following the line on the page as needed.
• Repeat with the remaining images.

sessions.title: Session B
learning_outcomes: Know that words are separated by spaces.
Use new words correctly in sentences.
Answer factual questions.
Use verbal and non-verbal communication appropriately.

activities.title: Words are separated by spaces
activities.content:
Describe what a word is, and why there are 
spaces between them
• Take out the read aloud book from 
yesterday's lesson.Choose a sentence to 
write on the board.
• Say: ÑIŋ diyaamoo bota taaliŋo le kono ŋa meŋ karaŋ ali ye. £ be naa Diyaamoo  
la, kenoo le la mennu be kumoolu teema. Niŋ be karanna, n ka kumoolu kiliŋ-kiliŋ 
karaŋ ne, katuŋ, kuma wo kuma ye koto le soto
• Point to a word in the sentence. Read the word and say its meaning.

• Point to the space after the word.
• Say: Kenoo meŋ be kumoolu teema, a ye a yitandi n na le ko, kumoolu taradulaa 
aniŋ kuma doo datidulaa
• Point to the following word in the sentence. Read the word and say its meaning.
• Say: Kenoo kumoolu teema, wo le ke I maakoyi ka a karaŋ noo. Niŋ i ye diyaamoolu   
siifaalu safee, i be kenoo ke la kumoolu teema.
• Write another sentence. Choose a volunteer to help demonstrate on the new 
sentence.
• Say: Ali ali bulukondiŋo laa kumoo duma. Saayiŋ kuma koteŋ yitandi n na. Ì be a 
yitandi la n na ñaadii le ko kumoolu maŋ ke kiliŋ ti. (Jaabiri kendoo;)-Kenoo be ì 
teema le
• Pick up the book. Walk around the room. Ask 3 pupils to find a space between two 
words, and put their fingers on it.

activities.title: How to read – track with a finger
activities.content:
Teach how to track words with a finger
• Point to the pictures of the boy and girl in 
the Pupil Book.
• Say: Ñiŋ mu ( MUSAA) le ti. Ñiŋ mu (FAATUMATA) le ti. Ñiŋ tunkuŋo kono ¥ ¢ be 
kuu jamaa le karanna ì la kuwo to.
• Say: Ali ali bulukondiŋo loo (MUSAA) kumoo koto, Musaa la nataaloo koto. ali 
bulukondiŋo loo (FAATUMATA) kumoo koto, FAATUMATA la nataaloo koto."
• Point to the following activity in the Pupil Book (matching activity).
• Ask pupils to point to MUSAA on the left side, then point to the matching name on 
the right side. Repeat with (FAATUMAT)
• Point to the following activity in the Pupil Book (box with boy and girl names).
• Ask pupils to say the first name in the left column, then point to the matching 
name in the row.
• Continue in the same way with each row.

activities.title: Read a sentence
activities.content:
Read a sentence using sight words
• Say:  Ŋa Faatumata je ñiŋ kayitoo kono santo. Saayiŋ ŋa kumakutoo le je! Ñiŋ 
kumakutoo ka a fo le ko, (a je). Baawoo ŋà Faatumata ñiŋ kumakutoo loŋ ne, ñiŋ 
nataaloolu ka meŋ fo, n si ì karaŋ noo le. 
• Point to the first picture sentence on the page in the Pupil Book. Ask pupils to 
name the picture on the right.
• Read the picture sentence aloud to pupils, showing them how you point to the 

pictures/word with your finger as you read.
• Continue to the next picture sentence. Ask pupils to point to the boy.
• Point to pictures or words as you read. (MUSAA) ye baa je) 
• Remind pupils that "je" means "to observe" or "to see." 
• Make a gesture to demonstrate seeing. Then, ask pupils to read the picture 
sentence again together.
• Say: Saayiŋ ali ye jumaa le je duuma? Ali ŋà ǹ bulukondiŋolu loo diyaamoo kaŋ, ŋà 
diyaamoo ñiŋ karaŋ ñoola. Faatumata ye taabuloo je   
• Say: Diyaamoo meŋ be a nooma jumaa le si a karaŋ noo? 
• Continue calling on pupils to read the picture sentences until the end of the page.

activities.title: Describe differences
activities.content:
Talk about the differences between objects Point to the next activity in the Pupil 
Book.
• Say: Ali ŋà ǹ bulukondiŋolu loo nataali foloo koto. Ali ye munne je? Ali ye siiraŋo je 
le baŋ meŋ ka naa ñiŋ nooma?"
• Point to the next picture in the row. 
• Say: "Haa, ninsoo!  munne ye niisoo niŋ saajiyo fata?"
• Continue with other illustrations.

activities.title: Draw shapes
activities.content:
Practice drawing common shapes
• Ask pupils to trace each shape in the Pupil Book with one finger.
• Ask pupils to try to draw 3 of each shape in their exercise books. Depending on 
their comfort with writing and drawing, different pupils may focus on just one 
shape or draw many.

activities.title: How to read – track with a finger
activities.content:
Teach how to track words with a finger
• Say: "Niŋ n be karanna, n ka kumoolu kiliŋkiliŋ juubee le. Kuma wo kuma ye koto 
le soto. A kummaayaata le, ka kumoolu 
kiliŋkiliŋ karaŋ fahaamuroo kamma. Ka i 
bulukondiŋo loo kumoo kaŋ niŋ i be karanna, 
a ka i maakoyi le, i kana sawuŋ kuma la."
• Write a sentence on the board. Demonstrate how to track with your finger under 
each word as you read. Be sure to place and pause your finger under the specific 
word.
• Call on a pupil at random to describe what to do with a finger while reading.
• Call on 2 pupils to demonstrate tracking words of the sentence on the board while 
you read it aloud.

activities.title: Read aloud
activities.content:
Reread the following story aloud
• use the appropriate big book or supplementary illustrations if available

• Partway through the story, pause to show pupils how you track reading with your 
finger below each word you read as you read it. At the end of the line of text, make 
a big sweeping motion back to the start of the next line of text. Continue tracking 
with your finger.
• After demonstrating, complete the read aloud.

A baamaa ye a faamaa juubee, a ko, "ŋà ñiŋ sankee saŋ bii! Dukaree I bori sankee

Ñiŋ keta dindiŋ taaliŋo le ti, meŋ be dendiŋ kajee saasaa tankadiriñaa niŋ a jaarañaa

activities.title: Vocabulary – after reading
activities.content:
Check for vocabulary understanding
• Ask pupils if they heard the new vocabulary words during the read aloud.
• Call on 3-4 pupils to say what vocabulary word they heard and to say the meaning 
in their own words.
• Say: Saayiŋ ali ŋa kumoolu taa ŋà mennu karaŋ, ŋà diyaamoo dedaa.
• Give an example by using one of the words in a new sentence - one that is not in 
the pupil book or read aloud.
• For each other vocabulary word introduced before reading, ask a pupil to use the 
word in a new sentence. Have pupils act out a word, if appropriate. Congratulate, 
help, or correct the pupils, depending on the responses.

activities.title: Rapid review
activities.content:
Review tracking words with a finger
• Ask a volunteer pupil to tell you something you should do to be sure you don't 
skip words while reading. (Correct response - track the words with your finger, or 
follow under the words with your finger, etc.)
• Ask one pupil to demonstrate tracking for the class using the book.

Describe the difference between letter shapes
• Ask pupils to tell you what is different about the two shapes, the i and the j. Do not say the 
name of the letter - this is NOT an activity for pupils to learn letters, it is an activity for pupils 
to practice telling the difference between the shapes of the letters.
• Ask pupils to trace the shapes with their fingers.

activities.title: Read a sentence using sight words
activities.content:
Talk about the differences between objects
• Ask pupils to try to read the picture sentences using the sight words they learned previously. 
Monitor and help pupils as needed.
• After giving pupils an opportunity to read the sentences independently, call on a pupil at 
random to read the first sentence. Ask another pupil to read the second, then continue for 
each of the sentences. Ensure that pupils know the correct way to read each sentence.

activities.title: Comprehension questions— factual
activities.content:
Review the question word "Who" (" ")
• Read the question: 
• Say: Jumaa le ye Jaaralilaa kumandi biriŋ Aadama dindiŋ saasaata? Jaabiroo; 
Adama dindiŋ faamaa le ye Jaaralilaa kumandi biriŋ a saasaata.  
• Ask pupils to answer the question. Give them feedback. 
• Ask pupils if they can tell you what the question word "who""jumaa" is asking 
about. Call on one or two pupils to respond. Let them know if they are correct, or 
incorrect and why. (Response: the question word "who"'Jumaa" asks us the name 
of a someone or something alive)
• Teach pupils to use the question word "where"
• Tell pupils that they will learn a new question word today, " ." Tell pupils that 
they will use it to answer the next question.

Read the question: 
• Say: Niŋ I saasaata, I ka taa mintoo le?
• Say: Ñiŋ' kumoo meŋ mu 'mintoo' ti, ka a yitandi ǹ na le ko ǹ ñanta dulaa le yitandi 
la ǹ na jaabiroo kono waraŋ. 

Read the question: 
• Say: Aadama be nuŋ mintoo le biriŋ a baamaa niŋ a faamaa be a kumandi kaŋ?" 
Jaabiroo; (Aadama be nuŋ a la buŋo le kono biriŋ a faamaa niŋ a baamaa be a 
kumandi kaŋ)
• Say: Ali ŋa ǹ na miiroolu samba dulaa to ǹ ŋa dulaa meŋ meŋ na kuwo karaŋ nuŋ. 
Karaŋ kacaadaa ko le ko; a be laariŋ laaraŋo kaŋ ne hanii saayiŋ.
• Ask pupils to think about "where", or the place, that this happened.
• Call on pupils at random to respond.

sessions.title: Session A
learning_outcomes: Display mastery of key skills learned over the last four lessons: the parts of a book, spaces between words and tracking a finger under print.

activities.title: Assessment
activities.content:
Special assessment - assess week 1 skills:
• Know what the "cover " and "back " of the 
book means.
• Understand that words in print are 
separated by spaces. 
• Know that tracking a finger under a word 
helps keep track of where you are reading.

1. Know what the "cover" and "back" of the book means.
• Hand out pupil books
• Tell pupils to hold up their books and point to the "front". Give feedback and 
explain. Give more examples if needed. If you see any pupil struggling, make sure 
to support them in this skill during the next lessons.
• Tell pupils to hold up their books and point to the "back" of the book. Give 
feedback, and explain and give more examples if needed.

2. Understand that words in print are separated by spaces
• Ask pupils to turn to the first decodable story in their book. Show them the picture 
for the story, so they can find the story in the book. They will not be able to read 
this story yet, but that is alright. Do not ask them to read the story.
• Point to the "space" between the first two words in the story. Ask all pupils to put 
their finger on that space. Walk around and show them where to put their finger.
• Ask pupils to point to the next space in the story. Walk around to observe and give 
feedback.
• Ask pupils to raise their hand if they know what that space is for (why it's there). 
• Ask a volunteer to answer. Ask another pupil if the response is correct.
• Say: Kenoo meŋ be kumoolu teema, wo le ka a yitandi ko, wo kumoolu maŋ ke kiliŋ 
ti.
3. Know that tracking a finger under a word helps keep track of where you are 

reading
• Open a big book (any big book) to the first page. Ask pupils to watch and listen. 
Read the first sentence while pointing to (tracking) each word with your finger.
• Ask pupils what you were doing with your finger. Then ask them why you did that. 
Tell the pupil who responds if they are correct or not. Then repeat or say the 
correct response. (Possible response: I was tracking a finger under the words as I 
read them. Tracking with a finger helps you know where you are while reading, so 
you don't get confused or lost.)

Tantaŋo: Tan/ta/ŋo

activities.title: Short and long vowel sound
activities.content:
Hear and see the short vowel within a word
• Point to the first picture on the page of the Pupil Book.
• Say: I ye munne je?
• Ask one pupil to name what is in the picture. Repeat the correct word. If needed, 
help pupils understand the word by saying it in another language they know.
• Say: Ali ŋà ¥ buloolu kosi kumabuloolu ye mennu be kumoo kono (aba). Siiñaa jelu 
le mu, ali ye /a/ kulukaŋo moyi kumoo kono (aba) ali ŋà ¥ buloolu kosi kontenke.
• Touch the letter in the Pupil Book. Say the sound. If pupils struggle to hear and 
say the sound, help them by saying another word with that sound in your language 
or another language they know.
• Say: Ali ŋà kuma naalaa fo ñoola, (awa) Fo ali ye /a/ kulukaŋo moyi ñiŋ (awa) 
kumoo kono le? siiñaa jelu le mu ali ye a moyi?
• Say:  Saayiŋ, ite le ñanta a ke la, kumoo fo. Niŋ i be a fo kaŋ, i ye i bulukondiŋo loo 
/a/ kuloo koto.

Hear and see the long vowel within a word
• Point to the first picture in the next row on the Pupil Book page.
• Say: Moo wo Moo ñanta i bulukondiŋo loo la nataaloo koto "baa" i ye 
taamaaseeroo ke meŋ bala.
• Say: Ali ye munne je? A mu "baa'' le ti.
• Clap the syllables with the pupils. 
• Say: /a/ kulukaŋo fanaŋ si saba noo le. Wo le mu ñiŋ ti ko, niŋ ŋà a fo, ǹ si a foñaa 
sab fo a ye jamfa. Fo i ye kulumusu jaŋo/aa/ moyi kumoo kono le baŋ"baa"?  
• Write the word on the chalk board. Point to the long vowel. Ask pupils to point to 
the same vowel in their book. Ask pupils how many of the letters of the day they 
see next to each other. Answer: two
• Tell pupils that when they see two /a/ together, it makes a long sound /aa/. The 
long sound means that you stretch the sound longer when you say it.
• Demonstrate saying the short vowel sound and then the long vowel sound. Ask 
pupils to repeat. 

• Ensure that they can hear the difference between the short sound and the long 
(stretched) sound.
• Continue in the same way using the next picture. Look at it, say the word, clap the 
syllables and listen for the long vowel in the word.

During reading, stop to discuss places and times

the story?

activities.title: Assessment (individual assessment while the rest of the class reads in pairs)
activities.content:
Administer the assessment
• You will assess 10 pupils. While the whole class is reading in pairs, call one pupil 
to sit with you.
• Open the assessment booklet to the assessment for this week. 
• Show the pupil the 5 letters. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Show the pupil the 5 syllables. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).

• Do this for another 9 pupils (to complete all 10). Next week you will assess 10 
more pupils starting with the next pupil on the list.
Score the assessment - for each pupil
• Total the correct letters and syllables for each pupil - across the row. This gives a 
general sense of how the child is learning: 8-10 correct is good. 6-7 is developing. 
1-5 may indicate that the child is struggling. 
Score the assessment - for class progress
• Total the correct letters and syllables for the 10 pupils by adding each column. 
A total of 40-50 is good, 30-40 is developing, and less than 30 is a challenge. 
Consider reinforcement activities for skill areas that are less than 40.
Looking forward

beginning of the list.

activities.title: Reinforcement activities
activities.content:
NOTE 
Choose a reinforcement activity from the 
options below. Base your choice on the 
skill(s) your pupils found challenging in the 
assessment. The skill reinforced by the activity 
is in the activity name: "letter sounds" or 
"syllable blending".
Letter sounds - Can you think of a word?
• Use flashcards. Hold up a letter pupils have learned but need to practice. Ask a 
pupil to say the letter sound. Repeat the correct letter sound. Ask pupils to think 
of a word that starts with the sound. Calls on 5-10 pupils to share their words, 
then move on to the next letter.
Letter sounds - Letter zoom
• Ask pupils to turn to the table of letters at the back of the pupil book. Call a letter 
sound that pupils have already learned. Ask pupils to look at the letters in the 
table and quickly tap the letter that makes that sound. Repeat with additional 
letters that pupils have already learned. *TIP - start saying letter sounds at a 
speed that gets as many pupils to participate as possible, then gradually start 
saying letter sounds more quickly. 
Syllable blending - Whisper the syllable
• Use flashcards. Choose 3 consonants and 3 short or long vowels from the 
flashcards (try to use letters that pupils may struggle with or have forgotten). 
Hold up a consonant and say its sound. Hold up a short or long vowel and say its 
sound (or have pupils say the sound). Ask pupils to turn to a partner and quietly 
say the syllable  made by the who flashcards. When they agree on the syllable, 
have them raise their hands. Wait until most of the class has raised their hands. 
Call on a pair at random to say the syllable. If they are correct, give a clap of 
appreciation. Continue using flashcards to make 5-10 more syllables for pupils to 
say in pairs. 
Syllable blending - Phonics bingo

• Write 10 syllables on the blackboard that pupils have already learned. Read the 
items aloud once. Ask pupils to choose 3 of them to write in a notebook, paper, 
slate, or other place. Call one of the syllables at random. The first pupil to hear all 
3 of the syllables they wrote down raises their hand. If they can say all 3 correct 
items, they get a clap of appreciation from the class

activities.title: Assessment (individual assessment while the rest of the class reads in pairs)
activities.content:
Administer the assessment
• You will assess 10 pupils. While the whole class is reading in pairs, call one pupil 
to sit with you.
• Open the assessment booklet to the assessment for this week. 
• Show the pupil the 5 letters. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Show the pupil the 5 syllables. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Do this for another 9 pupils (to complete all 10). Next week you will assess 10 

more pupils starting with the next pupil on the list.
Score the assessment - for each pupil
• Total the correct letters and syllables for each pupil - across the row. This gives a 
general sense of how the child is learning: 8-10 correct is good. 6-7 is developing. 
1-5 may indicate that the child is struggling.
Score the assessment - for class progress
• Total the correct letters and syllables for the 10 pupils by adding each column. 
A total of 40-50 is good, 30-40 is developing, and less than 30 is a challenge. 
Consider reinforcement activities for skill areas that are less than 40.
Looking forward
• Next week, continue with the next 10 pupils on the list.
• Continue this way until all pupils are assessed, then start over again from the 
beginning of the list.

activities.title: Reinforcement activities
activities.content:
NOTE 
Choose a reinforcement activity from the 
options below. Base your choice on the skill(s) 
your pupils found challenging in the assessment. 
The skill reinforced by the activity is in the 
activity name: "letter sounds" or "syllable 
blending "
Letter sounds - Can you think of a word?
• Use flashcards. Hold up a letter pupils have learned but need to practice. Ask a 
pupil to say the letter sound. Repeat the correct letter sound. Ask pupils to think 
of a word that starts with the sound. Calls on 5-10 pupils to share their words, 
then move on to the next letter.

Letter sounds - Letter zoom
• Ask pupils to turn to the table of letters at the back of the pupil book. Call a letter 
sound that pupils have already learned. Ask pupils to look at the letters in the 
table and quickly tap the letter that makes that sound. Repeat with additional 
letters that pupils have already learned. *TIP - start saying letter sounds at a 
speed that gets as many pupils to participate as possible, then gradually start 
saying letter sounds more quickly.

Syllable blending - Whisper the syllable
• Use flashcards. Choose 3 consonants and 3 short or long vowels from the 
flashcards (try to use letters that pupils may struggle with or have forgotten). 
Hold up a consonant and say its sound. Hold up a short or long vowel and say its 
sound (or have pupils say the sound). Ask pupils to turn to a partner and quietly 
say the syllable made by the who flashcards. When they agree on the syllable, 
have them raise their hands. Wait until most of the class has raised their hands. 
Call on a pair at random to say the syllable. If they are correct, give a clap of 
appreciation. Continue using flashcards to make 5-10 more syllables for pupils to 
say in pairs.

Syllable blending - Phonics bingo
• Write 10 syllables on the blackboard that pupils have already learned. Read the 
items aloud once. Ask pupils to choose 3 of them to write in a notebook, paper, 
slate, or other place. Call one of the syllables at random. The first pupil to hear all 
3 of the syllables they wrote down raises their hand. If they can say all 3 correct 
items, they get a clap of appreciation from the class.

activities.title: Word matching
activities.content:
• Ask pupils to put their fingers under the first word in the word list for the activity 
in the pupil book. Read the first word.
• Say: Ñiŋ kumoo koto duŋ?
• Ask for a volunteer to tell say the meaning of the word. Then, ask pupils to point 
to the picture on the page that matches that word. Ask all pupils to point to the 
next word in the list and whisper read it to themselves. Call on a pupil at random 
to read the word for the class. Ask all pupils to point to the picture that matches 
the word.
• Continue the activity to the end of the word list, helping pupils that get stuck.

activities.title: Word building
activities.content:
Use syllables to build given words
• Tell pupils they will write words using the syllables in the box. 
• Say: N be n miira kaŋ kumoo la. Kumoo ñiŋ mu '' caaboo ''. I lamoyi kuuke aduŋ I 
ye buloo kosi ñiŋ kulukaŋo ye naa.
• Ask pupils to point to the first syllable in the word on the page in their Pupil Books. 
Then, write the syllable on the board.
• Continue asking pupils to point to the syllables in the word until the full word is 
written on the board.
• Say: Kumoo ñiŋ mu '' caaboo ''. Saayiŋ ŋà kumoo bee safe le. Ali ŋà a karaŋ ñoola. 
(Pupils read the word)
• Say the first word below and clap the syllables with pupils. Give pupils time to find 
the syllables of the word and point to them in their book, then write them to form 
the word in their copy books. After all pupils have written the word, say the next 
word. Continue with the rest of the words. Words: caaloo caa/loo, baaba: baa/
ba, caaboo: caa/boo, cuuboo; cuu/boo, cika, ci/ka
• Use syllables to build new words
• Say: " Saayiŋ, m lafita le ali ye ali fansuŋ kumoolu dedaa!
• Ask pupils to use any of the syllables in the pupil book to make another word that 
they know and write it in their copy books.
• When pupils are finished, ask them to turn to a partner to share the word they 
made.

activities.content:

• Point to the small letter "d" on the alphabet poster or on the board.
• Say: Ñiŋ ne mu ǹ na kulu kutoo ti bii. Ñiŋ kuloo ka /d/ kulu kaŋo le fo. Ali ŋà fo 
ñoola /d/
• Ask pupils to say the sound with you (no more than 2 times).

• Point to the capital letter " D" on the alphabet poster or on the board.
• Say: Ñiŋ mu a te kulukiliŋo le ti. A te fanaŋ ka /d/ kulu kaŋo fo. £ ka je te¿ ne 
diyaamu temberiŋo waraŋ toolu dati duula to.
• Point to the small letter "l" on the alphabet poster or on the board again.
• Say: Waati jamaa ¥ ka a je kumoolu kono te¿ ne.
Keyword picture study
• Say: Ali ye munne je?
• Call on 1-2 pupils to name what they see in the picture.
• Say the keyword. Touch the letter of the day in the keyword in the pupil book.Say 
the sound. 
• Say: ÿà ñiŋ kumoo fo ñoola "daboo." Fo ali ye /d/ kulukaŋo moyi le "daboo" kumoo 
Kono?
• Ask pupils to touch the letter and say the word again.
Keyword analysis (Pupil Book Box #1) 
• Write the keyword from Box #1 on the board. 
• Point to the keyword.
• Say: Kumoo mu "Laaloo"
• Point to the letter (under the keyword). Read it and show pupils how the letter is part 
of the keyword.

activities.title: Read syllables
activities.content:
Use the new letter sound to read syllables (Pupil Book Box #2)
• Write the Box #2 syllable column on the board. 
• Point to the first syllable. Cover the "a" and show the "d ".
• Say: Munne mu ñiŋ kulukaŋo ti? (pupils respond " l") 
• Cover the "d " and show the "a".
• Say: Munne mu ñiŋ kulukaŋo ti? (pupils respond "a")
• Say:  Ali si kulukaŋolu karaŋ ñoola, ali ye ì cooki ñoola, ka kumabuloolu fo. Saayiŋ 
ali ŋà kulukaŋolu fo ñoola. /d/ /a/: "da"
• Continue in this way for the other syllables. Ask pupils to do the others. They will 
say  each sound, and then the syllable. 
• After the pupils have read all the syllables together, give them 1 minute to try 
reading the syllables independently again from their books.
Rapid syllable reading (Pupil Book Box #3)

• Write the first column of Box #3 on the board.
• Ask pupils, all together, to read down the column on the board. 
• Write each additional column, one at a time. Have pupils read the syllables in each 
column.
• Point to 5 syllables randomly. Ask the whole class to read each one quickly as you 
point to it.

activities.title: Read words
activities.content:
Blending syllables to read words
• Write the first word on the chalkboard and help pupils find it in their books.
• Say: Ali i lamoyi, ali ye a juubee. N be na kumabuloolu fo la, ka ì cooki, ka ì ke kumoo 
ti.
• Model the blending process by reading each syllable, then blending the syllables 
together to read the word.
• Say: Ali ŋà a kata ñoola.
• Read the same syllables and the word, but this time with the pupils. Then ask the 
pupils to try the same word by themselves.
• Say: Saayiŋ ali ye a loŋ ne ali ñanta meŋ kela. Ali kuma doolu karaŋ ali ali la bukoo 
kono wo ñaama. Kumabulu foloo
• Call on 4 pupils at random to read one of the words using the blending process - 
reading the syllables, then the word. Provide help if needed.

activities.content:

page and saying the page number.
• Say: Ali naataloo juubee. Ali ye munne je? Ali ye a miira ñiŋ taaliŋo be kela munne kuu 
le ti?
• Give pupils a moment to think, then invite them to share their predictions with a 
partner. Call on 2 pupils at random and ask for their predictions.

activities.title: Reason to read
activities.content:
Think about why you want to read the story
• Say: Saayiŋ, ali be taaliŋo karanna ali faŋ ye ali la bukoolu kono. Ali si kumoolu 
mennu be taaliŋo kono karaŋ noo le katuŋ kumoolu be dedariŋ niŋ kulu le la ŋà 
mennu karaŋ nuŋ.
• Say: Laalo niŋ Baaba taata wuloo kono. Biriŋ Baaba pareeta a taata Laalo la buŋo 
kono bari a maŋ Laalo tara jee. Ali ŋà a karaŋ ka a loŋ Laalo be daameŋ nuŋ?

karaŋ.

activities.title: Decodable story reading – Independent
activities.content:
Pupils read aloud in the book independently
• Ask pupils to read the decodable story independently. Do NOT read it aloud for them. 
They should whisper read (read quietly), putting their finger under each word as they 
read it. If pupils finish reading early, they can read the story again with a partner.
• Walk around the classroom while pupils read. Help pupils use the skills they have 
learnt to read words. They should blend sounds to read syllables, and blend syllables 
to read words.

activities.title: Comprehension – Prediction check
activities.content:
Check prediction based on picture
• Ask pupils to remember the predictions they made before they read the story. Give 
them a moment to think. Ask them to raise their hands if their predictions were what 
happened in the story.
• Remind the class what the volunteer pupils predicted before they read the story. Ask 
the pupils if those predictions were what happened.

activities.title: Writing – Letters
activities.content:
Pupils practice writing the letter
• Ask pupils to locate the letter "d" in a word in the decodable story. 
• Call on 2 pupils at random to share the words they found.
• Write the letter "d" on the board (1/3 meter tall).
• Air write the letter (use a straight arm) and describe how to write the letter as you 
do it. Invite pupils to air write with you and say the sound. Watch them as they do it.
• Ask pupils to write the letter with a finger on their desks while saying the sound of 
the letter.
• Ask pupils to take out their exercise books and write the letter "d"5 times.
• If some pupils finish early, tell them to draw a picture of something that begins with 
the sound /l/.

activities.title: Vocabulary – after reading
activities.content:
Check for vocabulary understanding
• Ask pupils if they heard the new vocabulary words during the read aloud.
• Call on 3-4 pupils to say what vocabulary word they heard and to say the meaning 
in their own words.
• Say:  Ali ŋà kumatembediriŋ kutoo lu deda niŋ ǹ na kumoolu ŋà mennu karaŋ nuŋ.
• Give an example by using one of the words in a new sentence - a sentence that is 
not in the pupil book or read aloud.

word in a new sentence. Have pupils act out a word, if appropriate. Congratulate, 
help, or correct the pupils, depending on the responses.

activities.title: Assessment (individual assessment while the rest of the class reads in pairs)
activities.content:
Administer the assessment
• You will assess 10 pupils. While the whole class is reading in pairs, call one pupil to 
sit with you.
• Open the assessment booklet to the assessment for this week. 

• Show the pupil the 5 letters. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Show the pupil the 5 syllables. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Do this for another 9 pupils (to complete all 10). Next week you will assess 10 more 
pupils starting with the next pupil on the list (pupil # 11).
Score the assessment - for each pupil
• Total the correct letters and syllables for each pupil - across the row. This gives a 
general sense of how the child is learning: 8-10 correct is good. 6-7 is developing. 
1-5 may indicate that the child is struggling. 
Score the assessment - for class progress
• Total the correct letters and syllables for the 10 pupils by adding each column. A 
total of 40-50 is good, 30-40 is developing, and less than 30 is a challenge. Consider 
reinforcement activities for skill areas that are less than 40.
Looking forward
• Next week, continue with the next 10 pupils on the list (pupils #11-20).
• Continue this way until all pupils are assessed, then start over again from the 
beginning of the list.

activities.title: Reinforcement activities
activities.content:
NOTE

Letter sounds - Can you think of a word?
• Use flashcards. Hold up a letter pupils have learned but need to practice. Ask a 
pupil to say the letter sound. Repeat the correct letter sound. Ask pupils to think 
of a word that starts with the sound. Calls on5-10 pupils to share their words, 
then move on to the next letter.
Letter sounds - Letter zoom
• Ask pupils to turn to the table of letters at the back of the pupil book. Call a letter 
sound that pupils have already learned. Ask pupils to look at the letters in the 
table and quickly tap the letter that makes that sound. Repeat with additional 
letters that pupils have already learned. *TIP - start saying letter sounds at a 
speed that gets as many pupils to participate as possible, then gradually start 
saying letter sounds more quickly. 
Syllable blending - Whisper the syllable
• Use flashcards. Choose 3 consonants and 3 short or long vowels from the 
flashcards (try to use letters that pupils may struggle with or have forgotten). 
Hold up a consonant and say its sound. Hold up a short or long vowel and say its 
sound (or have pupils say the sound). Ask pupils to turn to a partner and quietly 
say the syllable made by the who flashcards. When they agree on the syllable, 
have them raise their hands. Wait until most of the class has raised their hands. 
Call on a pair at random to say the syllable. If they are correct, give a clap of 
appreciation. Continue using flashcards to make 5-10 more syllables for pupils to 
say in pairs. 

Syllable blending - Phonics bingo
• Write 10 syllables on the blackboard that pupils have already learned. Read the 
items aloud once. Ask pupils to choose 3 of them to write in a notebook, paper, 
slate, or other place. Call one of the syllables at random. The first pupil to hear all 
3 of the syllables they wrote down raises their hand. If they can say all 3 correct 
items, they get a clap of appreciation from the class.

activities.title: Assessment (individual assessment while the rest of the class reads in pairs)
activities.content:
Administer the assessment

to sit with you.

• Show the pupil the 5 letters. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Show the pupil the 5 syllables. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).

• Do this for another 9 pupils (to complete all 10).Next week you will assess 10 more 
pupils starting with the next pupil on the list (pupil # 11).
Score the assessment - for each pupil
• Total the correct letters and syllables for each pupil - across the row. This gives a 
general sense of how the child is learning: 8-10 correct is good. 6-7 is developing. 
1-5 may indicate that the child is struggling. 
Score the assessment - for class progress
• Total the correct letters and syllables for the 10 pupils by adding each column. 
A total of 40-50 is good, 30-40 is developing, and less than 30 is a challenge. 
Consider reinforcement activities for skill areas that are less than 40.
Looking forward
• Next week, continue with the next 10 pupils on the list (pupils #11-20).
• Continue this way until all pupils are assessed, then start over again from the 
beginning of the list.

activities.title: Reinforcement activities
activities.content:
NOTE
Choose a reinforcement activity from the 
options below. Base your choice on the 
skill(s) your pupils found challenging in 
the assessment. The skill reinforced by 
the activity is in the activity name: "letter 
sounds" or "syllable blending".
Letter sounds - Can you think of a word?
• Use flashcards. Hold up a letter pupils have learned but need to practice. Ask a 
pupil to say the letter sound. Repeat the correct letter sound. Ask pupils to think 
of a word that starts with the sound. Calls on5-10 pupils to share their words, 
then move on to the next letter.
Letter sounds - Letter zoom
• Ask pupils to turn to the table of letters at the back of the pupil book. Call a letter 
sound that pupils have already learned. Ask pupils to look at the letters in the 
table and quickly tap the letter that makes that sound. Repeat with additional 
letters that pupils have already learned. *TIP - start saying letter sounds at a 
speed that gets as many pupils to participate as possible, then gradually start 
saying letter sounds more quickly. 
Syllable blending - Whisper the syllable
• Use flashcards. Choose 3 consonants and 3 short or long vowels from the 
flashcards (try to use letters that pupils may struggle with or have forgotten). 
Hold up a consonant and say its sound. Hold up a short or long vowel and say its 
sound (or have pupils say the sound). Ask pupils to turn to a partner and quietly 
say the syllable made by the who flashcards. When they agree on the syllable, 
have them raise their hands. Wait until most of the class has raised their hands. 
Call on a pair at random to say the syllable. If they are correct, give a clap of 
appreciation. Continue using flashcards to make 5-10 more syllables for pupils to 
say in pairs. 
Syllable blending - Phonics bingo

• Write 10 syllables on the blackboard that pupils have already learned. Read the 
items aloud once. Ask pupils to choose 3 of them to write in a notebook, paper, 
slate, or other place. Call one of the syllables at random. The first pupil to hear all 
3 of the syllables they wrote down raises their hand. If they can say all 3 correct 
items, they get a clap of appreciation from the class.

activities.title: Word matching
activities.content:
• Ask pupils to put their fingers under the first word in the word list for the activity 
in the pupil book. Read the first word.
• Say: What does this word mean? Ñiŋ kumoo munne firiŋ?
• Ask for a volunteer to tell say the meaning of the word. Then, ask pupils to point 
to the picture on the page that matches that word. Ask all pupils to point to the 
next word in the list and whisper read it to themselves. Call on a pupil at random 
to read the word for the class. Ask all pupils to point to the picture that matches 
the word.
• Continue the activity to the end of the word list, helping pupils that get stuck.

activities.title: Word building
activities.content:
Use syllables to build given words
• Tell pupils they will write words using the syllables in the box. 
• Say: Ǹ be n miira kaŋ kumoo le la. Kumoo mu ''naanaa'' le ti. Ali ŋà juubee aniŋ ŋà 
ǹ buloolu kosi kumabuloo lu ye /naa/ /naa/.
• Ask pupils to point to the first syllable in the word on the Lesson 20 page in their 
Pupil Books. Then, write the syllable on the board.
• Continue asking pupils to point to the syllables in the word until the full word is 
written on the board.
• Say: Kumoo Mu ''naanaa'' le ti. Saayiŋ ŋà kumoo muumee safe le. Ali ŋà a karaŋ 
ñoola.
• Say the first word below and clap the syllables with pupils. Give pupils time to find 
the syllables of the word and point to them in their book, then write them to form 
the word in their copy books. After all pupils have written the word, say the next 
word. Continue with the rest of the words.
• Words: Naana: Naa/na, daboo: da/boo, naanoo: naa/noo, baci: ba/ci, neene: 
nee/ne, nenoo: ne/noo, coodi: coo/di, kuloo: ku/loo
Use syllables to build new words
• Say: Saayiŋ, I lafita le ali ye ali fansuŋ kumoolu dedaa!.
• Ask pupils to use any of the syllables in the pupil book to make another word that 
they know and write it in their copy books.
• Turn and talk: When pupils are finished, ask them to turn to a pupil next to them 
to share the word they made.

• Say each word below. Pupils put a hand up if they hear the sound at the end of the

Laalo, kilo, maanoo, Lalla, Laamini, lodoo, coodi

activities.title: Letter and keyword
activities.content:
Teach the letter
• Point to the small letter   " l " on the alphabet poster or on the board.
• Say: Ñiŋ ne mu ǹ na kulukutoo ti bii. Ñiŋ kuloo le ka /l / kulukaŋo fo. Ali ŋà fo ñoola 
/ l/
• Ask pupils to say the sound with you (no more than 2 times).

• Point to the capital letter "L" on the alphabet poster or on the board.
• Say: A te le mu wo kulu kiliŋo ti. A te le fanaŋ ka kulukaŋo /l/ fo. Niŋ a naa ta 
kumabuloo datidulaa waraŋ too, Ǹ ka je teŋ ne.
• Point to the small letter "l" on the alphabet poster or on the board again.
• Say: Waati jamaalu, ǹ be a je la teŋ ne ñiŋ kumoolu kono.''

Keyword picture study
• Say: I ye munne je?
• Call on 1-2 pupils to name what they see in the picture.
• Say the keyword. Touch the letter of the day in the keyword in the pupil book. Say 
the sound. 
• Say: Ali kumoo fo n nooma: Laalo. A fo, Kotenke: / Laalo/'. I ye a moyi /l/ "Laalo'' 
kono?
• Ask pupils to touch the letter and say the word again. 

Keyword analysis (Pupil Book Box #1)
• Write the keyword from Box #1 on the board. 
• Point to the keyword.
• Say: Kumoo mu '' Laalo " le ti.
• Point to the syllable (under the keyword). Read it and show pupils how the syllable 
is part of the keyword.
• Point to the letter (under the syllable). Read it and show pupils how the letter is 
part of the syllable.

activities.title: Read syllables
activities.content:
Use the new letter sound to read syllables (Pupil Book Box #2)
· Write the Box #2 syllable column on the board. 
·   Point to the first syllable. Cover the "a" and show the "l".
·   Say: Ñiŋ mu kulukaŋ jumaa le ti? (pupils respond "l")
·   Cover the "l" and show the "a".
• Say: "Which sound is this?" (pupils respond "a"). Ñiŋ mu kulukaŋ jumaa le ti?" 
(pupils respond "a")
• Say: Ali si kulukaŋolu karaŋ ñoola, wo koolaa ali ye ì coki ñoola ka kumabuloo fo. 
Saayiŋ ali kulukaŋolu karaŋ ñoola.'' Ali si kuloolu karaŋ I faŋ ye aniŋ ali ye ì coki 
ñoola ka kumabuloo dedaa. Wo koolaa ali ye kulukaŋo karaŋ ñoola kotenke ka ì 
coki ñoola ka kumabuloolu dedaa. / l/ /a/,"la''
• Continue in this way for the other syllables. Ask pupils to do the others. They will 
say each sound, and then the syllable. 
• After the pupils have read all the syllables together, give them 1 minute to try 
reading the syllables independently again from their books.

Rapid syllable reading (Pupil Book Box #3)
• Write the first column of Box #3 on the board.
• Ask pupils, all together, to read down the column on the board. 
• Write each additional column, one at a time. Have pupils read the syllables in each 
column.
• Point to 5 syllables randomly. Ask the whole class to read each one quickly as you 
point to it.

activities.title: Read words
activities.content:
Blending syllables to read words
• Write the first word on the chalkboard and help pupils find it in their books.
• Say: Ali i lamoyi kuuke ali ye a juubee. N be kumabuloo karanna le ŋa na coki 
ñoola ka kumoo dedaa." 
• Model the blending process by reading each syllable, then blending the syllables 
together to read the word.
• Say: Ali ŋà a kata ŋà a juubee.''
• Read the same syllables and the word, but this time with the pupils. Then ask the 
pupils to try the same word by themselves.
• Say: Saayiŋ I ye a loŋ ne I be muŋ kela. Wo sila kiliŋo ñaama, saferi timmmariŋolu 
doolu karaŋ I la bukoo kono. Meŋ Foloo ta, kumabuloo karaŋ wo koolaa I ye 
kumoo fo. Bula a nooma ka I bulu kondiŋo loo a kaŋ.'' (Monitor and help pupils.)
• Call on 4 pupils at random to read one of the words using the blending process - 
reading the syllables, then the word. Provide help if needed.

ye. Bii ŋà ǹ lamoyi kutamaa la.

• Say: Ǹ be naa kumoo waraŋ diyaamoo le fo la, Ali si ì lamoyi baake.
• [A ka taa marisewo to]
• [A bota marisewo to.]

Answer: Ñiŋ kuma fuloolu ye yitandiroo ke feŋo la meŋ keta nuŋ aniŋ meŋ be keeriŋ 
saayiŋ Diyaamoo foloo ye a yitandi ko a be keakaŋ saayiŋ. Fulanjaŋo ye a yitandi ko 
a keta le nuŋ.
• Say: Diyaamoo waraŋ kuma jumaa le ye a yitandi ko ŋà meŋ je nataaloo kono?
• Call 1-2 learners to give similar example of my language rule and explain what it 
means. Focus on my language examples in pupils' examples.

activities.title: Vocabulary – Before reading
activities.content:
Teach and discuss vocabulary
• Write the vocabulary on the board (but not the definitions). Ask pupils what they 
know about each one.

• Discuss the word meaning, using gestures or illustrations to support understanding. 
If needed, help pupils understand the word by saying it in another language they 
know. 
Laalo laala

activities.title: Comprehension - Prediction
activities.content:
Prediction based on picture
• Help pupils find the decodable text of the day in their Pupil Books by holding up 
the page and saying the page number.
• Say: Nataaloo juubee! I ye, munne je? I ye a miira ko ñiŋ taaliŋ be kela, munne ti?'
• Give pupils a moment to think, then invite them to share their predictions with a 
partner. Call on 2 pupils at random and ask for their predictions.

activities.title: Reason to read
activities.content:
Think about why you want to read the story
• Say: Saayiŋ I damma le be taaliŋo karanna I la bukoo kono. I be kumoolu karanna 
noo le taaliŋo kono katu ì be saferiŋ niŋ kumabuloo lu le la ŋà mennu karaŋ fo ka 
paree.''
• Say:  Laalo niŋ Baaba taata wuloo kono. Biriŋ Baaba pareeta a taata Laalo la buŋo 
kono bari a maŋ Laalo tara jee. Ali ŋà a karaŋ ka a loŋ Laalo be daameŋ nuŋ?
• Click or tap here to enter text.
• Say: Sembe kuwo la I ye meŋ loŋ kuloolu to aniŋ kumabuloolu to I ye taaaliŋo 
karaŋ I faŋ ye. Niŋ I be a karankaŋ, I bulukondiŋo loo kuma wo kuma koto waati 
wo waati.''

activities.title: Decodable story reading – Independent
activities.content:
Pupils read aloud in the book independently
• Ask pupils to read the decodable story independently. Do NOT read it aloud for 
them. They should whisper read (read quietly), putting their finger under each 
word as they read it. If pupils finish reading early, they can read the story again 
with a partner.
• Walk around the classroom while pupils read. Help pupils use the skills they 
have learnt to read words. They should blend sounds to read syllables, and blend 
syllables to read words.

activities.title: Comprehension – Prediction check
activities.content:
Check prediction based on picture

• Ask pupils to remember their predictions from before they read the story. Give 
them a moment to think. Ask them to raise their hands if their predictions were 
what happened in the story.
• Remind the class what the volunteer pupils predicted before they read the story. 
Ask the pupils if those predictions were what happened.

activities.title: Writing – Letters
activities.content:
• Ask pupils to locate the letter "f" in a word in the decodable story. Call on 2 
pupils at random to share the words they found.
• Write the letter "l" on the board (1/3 meter tall).
• Air write the letter (use a straight arm) and describe how to write the letter as 
you do it. Invite pupils to air write with you and say the sound. Watch them as 
they do it.
• Ask pupils to write the letter with a finger on their desks while saying the sound of 
the letter.
• Ask pupils to take out their exercise books and write the letter "l" 5 times.
• If some pupils finish early, tell them to draw a picture of something that begins 
with the sound /l/.

Duwoo, ñaŋo, Kacandiŋo

• Ask pupils to do a thumbs up if they hear one of the new vocabulary words during

• Show the picture that goes with the story as you read aloud. Or, if you have the

• While reading, pause to think aloud and talk to pupils about the story at key 
moments such as when you come to a vocabulary word the pupils just learnt or

activities.title: Vocabulary – after reading
activities.content:
Check for vocabulary understanding
• Ask pupils if they heard the new vocabulary words during the read aloud.
• Call on 3-4 pupils to say what vocabulary word they heard and to say the meaning 
in their own words.
• Say:  ''Ali ŋà munafaŋ kumoolu la ŋà mennu karaŋ kabo diyaamu kuto kono.''
• Give an example by using one of the words in a new sentence - a sentence that is 
not in the pupil book or read aloud.
• For each other vocabulary word introduced before reading, ask a pupil to use the 
word in a new sentence. Have pupils act out a word, if appropriate. Congratulate, 
help, or correct the pupils, depending on the responses.
• Remind pupils that they can use these words anytime throughout the day. 
Encourage pupils to share the words with their families at home.

activities.content:
Pupils read in pairs
• Ask pupils to read the decodable story in pairs. Encourage pupils to help each 
other read challenging words.
• Walk around the room while pupils read. Encourage pupils to use skills they have 
learnt to read words. They should blend sounds to read syllables, and blend

activities.title: Comprehension – making connections
activities.content:
Ask comprehension questions
• Call on a pupil randomly to answer the following question:
• Question 1: Munne ye a tinna I ye a miira ko kacoo laf i ta ñaŋo dedaa la? 
Answer: Katu ko kacoo laf i ta ñaŋo le dedaa la I si a je a ye dulaa soto I be I 
laa la daameŋ
• Question 2: Munne kummaayaata Duwoo ye ka a ke .? Answer: Duwoo suulata 
ka ñaŋo dedaa.
• After each question, call on a pupil randomly to share their answer to the 
question. Discuss their answers with the class. Help the pupils think about what 
is in the text or picture, as well as their own experiences, to reflect on what may 
have given them that idea.
Make text-to-self connections
• Say: ''Niŋ ŋà taaliŋo karaŋ, a ka ǹ hakiloo bulandi niŋ feŋ ne la meŋ keta ntoolu 
faŋolu la buluwo kono nuŋ.'' Saayiŋ, ali ì miira ǹiŋ na.
• Say: Saayiŋ i miira ñiŋ na, fo I niŋ I baarimusoo wala I baarinkee nene siita le ka 
moo la kuwoo kacaa?
• Ask pupils to turn to a partner to share their answers.
• Call on a pupil randomly to share their answer to the question. Discuss their 
answer with the class. Help the pupils think about how the story relates to their 
own lives and how they can use their own experiences to understand the story.

• Ask pupils to take out their exercise books.
• Ask pupils to draw or write about the text-to-self connection they made to the

Prediction based on picture

partner. Call on 2 pupils at random and ask for their predictions.

Think about why you want to read the story
• Say: Saayiŋ, ite damma le be taaliŋo karanna I la bukoo kono. I si kumoolu karaŋ

activities.title: Decodable story reading – Independent
activities.content:
Pupils read aloud in the book independently

(read quietly), putting their finger under each word as they read it. If pupils finish 
reading early, they can read the story again with a partner.

have learnt to read words. They should blend sounds to read syllables, and blend 
syllables to read words.

activities.title: Comprehension – Prediction check
activities.content:
Check prediction based on picture

them a moment to think. Ask them to raise their hands if their predictions were 
what happened in the story.
• Remind the class what the volunteer pupils predicted before they read the story. 
Ask the pupils if those predictions were what happened.

activities.title: Writing – Letters
activities.content:
Check prediction based on picture
• Ask pupils to locate the letter "l" in a word in the decodable story. Call on 2 pupils 

at random to share the words they found.
• Write the letter "l" on the board (1/3 meter tall).
• Air write the letter (use a straight arm) and describe how to write the letter as 
you do it. Invite pupils to air write with you and say the sound. Watch them as 
they do it.
• Ask pupils to write the letter with a finger on their desks while saying the sound of 
the letter.
• Ask pupils to take out their exercise books and write the letter "l" 5 times.
• If some pupils finish early, tell them to draw a picture of something that begins 
with the sound /l/.

activities.title: Comprehension – making connections
activities.content:
Ask comprehension questions
• Call on pupils randomly to answer the following questions:
• Question 1: Munne ye a tinna I ye a miira ko kacoo laf i ta ñaŋo dedaa la? 
Answer: Katu ko kacoo laf ita ñaŋo le dedaa la I si a je a ye dulaa soto I be I

ka ñaŋo dedaa.
• After each question, call on a pupil randomly to share their answer to the 
question.   Discuss their answers with the class. Help the pupils think about what 
is in the text or picture, as well as their own experiences, to reflect on what may 
have given them that idea.
Make text-to-self connections
• Say: ''Saayiŋ i miira waatoo meŋ na duwoo be looriŋ samaa niŋ Foñoo koto. Fo 

samaa nene keta waraŋ fo foñoo nene feeta le nuŋ? I ye munne ke?'' [ jaabiri

• Ask pupils to turn to a partner to share their answers.
• Call on a pupil randomly to share their answer to the question. Discuss their 
answer with the class. Help the pupils think about how the story relates to their 
own lives and how they can use their own experiences to understand the story.

activities.title: Assessment: Before The Lesson
activities.content:
Prepare for the assessment
• Prepare an assessment page in a notebook. 
List all the pupils in the class in alphabetical

score".

Instruct pupils who are not being assessed

activities.title: Reason to Read
activities.content:
Think about why you want to read the story
• Tell pupils that they will be reading a story with a partner while you work with 
individual pupils.
• Say: ÿà loo je koobaadala musoo be jee . Ali ŋà a karaŋ fo ¥ si a loŋ meŋ be keeriŋ.
• Turn and talk: Ask pupils to turn to a pupil next to them to begin reading the story 
in their Pupil Books.
• Tell pupils that they will see a few words in the story missing. With their partners, 
they should choose which of the two options in parenthesis is the correct choice 
for the story.

activities.title: Assessment (individual assessment while the rest of the class reads in pairs)
activities.content:
Administer the assessment
• You will assess 10 pupils. While the whole class is reading in pairs, call one pupil 
to sit with you.
• Open the assessment booklet to the assessment for this week. 
• Show the pupil the 5 letters. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Show the pupil the 5 syllables. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Do this for another 9 pupils (to complete all 10).Next week you will assess 10 more 

pupils starting with the next pupil on the list (pupil # 11).
Score the assessment - for each pupil
• Total the correct letters and syllables for each pupil - across the row. This gives a 
general sense of how the child is learning: 8-10 correct is good. 6-7 is developing. 
1-5 may indicate that the child is struggling. 
Score the assessment - for class progress
• Total the correct letters and syllables for the 10 pupils by adding each column. 
A total of 40-50 is good, 30-40 is developing, and less than 30 is a challenge. 
Consider reinforcement activities for skill areas that are less than 40.
Looking forward
• Next week, continue with the next 10 pupils on the list (pupils #11-20).
• Continue this way until all pupils are assessed, then start over again from the 
beginning of the list.

activities.title: Reinforcement activities
activities.content:
NOTE 
Choose a reinforcement activity from the 
options below. Base your choice on the 
skill(s) your pupils found challenging in 
the assessment. The skill reinforced by 
the activity is in the activity name: "letter 
sounds" or "syllable blending".
Letter sounds - Can you think of a word?
• Use flashcards. Hold up a letter pupils have learned but need to practice. Ask a 
pupil to say the letter sound. Repeat the correct letter sound.Ask pupils to think of 
a word that starts with the sound. Calls on5-10 pupils to share their words, then 
move on to the next letter.
Letter sounds - Letter zoom
• Ask pupils to turn to the table of letters at the back of the pupil book. Call a letter 
sound that pupils have already learned. Ask pupils to look at the letters in the table 
and quickly tap the letter that makes that sound. Repeat with additional letters that 
pupils have already learned. *TIP - start saying letter sounds at a speed that gets 
as many pupils to participate as possible, then gradually start saying letter sounds 
more quickly. 
Syllable blending - Whisper the syllable
• Use flashcards. Choose 3 consonants and 3 short or long vowels from the flashcards 
(try to use letters that pupils may struggle with or have forgotten). Hold up a 
consonant and say its sound. Hold up a short or long vowel and say its sound (or 
have pupils say the sound). Ask pupils to turn to a partner and quietly say the 
syllable made by the flashcards. When they agree on the syllable, have them raise 
their hands. Wait until most of the class has raised their hands. Call on a pair at 
random to say the syllable. If they are correct, give a clap of appreciation. Continue 
using flashcards to make 5-10 more syllables for pupils to say in pairs. 
Syllable blending - Phonics bingo
• Write 10 syllables on the blackboard that pupils have already learned. Read the 
items aloud once. Ask pupils to choose 3 of them to write in a notebook, paper, 
slate, or other place. Call one of the syllables at random. The first pupil to hear all 
3 of the syllables they wrote down raises their hand. If they can say all 3 correct 

items, they get a clap of appreciation from the class.

activities.title: Word matching
activities.content:
Think about why you want to read the story
• Ask pupils to put their fingers under the first word in the word list for the activity 
in the pupil book. Read the first word.
• Say: ''Ñiŋ kumoo kotoo mu, munne ti?
• Ask for a volunteer to tell say the meaning of the word. Then, ask pupils to point 
to the picture on the page that matches that word.Ask all pupils to point to the 
next word in the list and whisper read it to themselves. Call on a pupil at random 
to read the word for the class. Ask all pupils to point to the picture that matches 
the word.
• Continue the activity to the end of the word list, helping pupils that get stuck.

activities.title: Word building
activities.content:
Use syllables to build given words
• Tell pupils they will write words using the syllables in the box. 
• Say: 'N be n miirakaŋ kumoo le la. Kumoo mu 'baloo' Ali ŋà buloo kosi: [ba/loo /]. 
Kumoomu' baloo' le ti. Ali ŋà kuntuŋ kuntuŋ ŋà buloo kosi:''ba/loo''
• Ask pupils to point to the first syllable in the word on the Lesson 20 page in their 
Pupil Book. Then, write the syllable on the board.
• Continue asking pupils to point to the syllables in the word until the full word is 
written on the board.
• Say: ''Kumoo mu" baloo" le ti. Saayiŋ ŋà kumoo muumee bee safe le. Ali ŋà karaŋ 
ñoola.'' (pupils read the word)
• Say the first word below and clap the syllables with pupils. Give pupils time to find 
the syllables of the word and point to them in their book, then write them to form 
the word in their copy books. After all pupils have written the word, say the next 
word. Continue with the rest of the words.
• Words: Laalo: Laa/lo, kilo: ki/lo, maanoo: maa/noo, Lala: La/la, Laamini: Laa/
mi/ni, lodoo: lo/doo, coodi: coo/di 
Use syllables to build new words
• Say: ''Saayiŋ N lafita ali ye a kata ŋa je niŋ a ye a tara ko ali si ali fansuŋ kumoolu 
dedaa!'' Saayiŋ, n lafita le ali ye a kata ka ali fasuŋ kumoolu dedaa!
• Ask pupils to use any of the syllables in the pupil book to make another word that 
they know and write it in their copy books.
• Turn and talk: When pupils are finished, ask them to turn to a pupil next to them 
to share the word they made.

kumoo kono''?

activities.title: Read syllables
activities.content:
Use the new letter sound to read syllables (Pupil Book Box #2)

• Point to the first syllable. Cover the "a" and show the "j"
• Say: Ñiŋ mu kulukaŋ juma le ti? (pupils respond "m")
• Cover the "m" and show the "a"
• Say: Ñiŋ mu kulukaŋ jumaa le ti? (pupils respond "a")
• Say: ''Ali si kulukaŋolu karaŋ noo ñoola wo koolaa ali ye ì coki ñoola ka kumabuloo 
dedaa.
•  Saayiŋ kulukaŋolu karaŋ aniŋ I ye ì coki ñoola:/ m / /a/, 'ma.' ''
• Continue in this way for the other syllables. Ask pupils to do the others.
• Continue in this way for the other syllables. Ask pupils to do the others. They will 
say each sound, and then the syllable. 
• After the pupils have read all the syllables together, give them 1 minute to try 
reading the syllables independently again from their books.

Rapid syllable reading (Pupil Book Box #3)
• Write the first column of Box #3 on the board.
• Ask pupils, all together, to read down the column on the board.

point to it.

• Say: ''Ali ì lamoyi kuuke ali ye a juubee. N be kumabuloo karanna ŋa naa 
kulukaŋolu coki ñoola ka kumoo dedaa
• Model the blending process by reading each syllable, then blending the syllables 
together to read the word.
• Say: Ali ŋà a kata ñoola.
• Read the same syllables and the word, but this time with the pupils. Then ask the 
pupils to try the same word by themselves.
• Say: ''Saayiŋ ali ye a loŋ ne ali ñanta meŋ kela. Ate keeñaa kili¿o ta ali ye kumaa 
doolu karaŋ ali la bukoolu kono. Foloo, kumabuloo karaŋ wo koolaa I ye kumoo fo. 
I bulukondiŋo coodi I ye bula a nooma.'' (Monitor and help pupils.)
• Call on 4 pupils at random to read one of the words using the blending process - 
reading the syllables, then the word. Provide help if needed.

Think about why you want to read the story
• Say: Saayiŋ I damma le be taaliŋo karanna I la bukoo kono. I be kumoolu karaŋ 
noo la le taaliŋo kono katu ko ì safe ta kumoolu kono le ǹ ŋa mennu karaŋ nuŋ.
• Say: Awa ye maani fee baa le soto. Dimaasi luŋo Awa taata a la maani faroo 
juubee. Ali ŋà a karaŋ fo ¥ si je munne be a la maani fee to aniŋ munne naata ke.
• Say: ''I ye meŋ loŋ wo taa I ye kuloolu niŋ kulukaŋolu karaŋ taaliŋo kono I faŋ ye. 
Niŋ I be a karaŋ kaŋ I bulukondiŋo coodi kuma wo kuma kaŋ.''

activities.title: Decodable story reading – Independent
activities.content:
Pupils read aloud in the book independently
• Ask pupils to read the decodable story independently. They should whisper read 
(read quietly), putting their finger under each word as they read it. If pupils finish 
reading early, they can read the story again with a partner.
• Walk around the classroom while pupils read. Help pupils use the skills they 
have learnt to read words. They should blend sounds to read syllables, and blend 
syllables to read words..

activities.title: Comprehension – Prediction check
activities.content:
Check prediction based on picture
• Ask pupils to remember their predictions from before they read the story. Give 
them a moment to think. Ask them to raise their hands if their predictions were 
what happened in the story.
• Remind the class what the volunteer pupils predicted before they read the story. 
Ask the pupils if those predictions were what happened.

activities.title: Writing – Letters
activities.content:
Pupils practice writing the letter
• Ask pupils to locate the letter "m" in a word in the decodable story. 
• Call on 2 pupils at  random to share the words they found.
• Write the letter "m" on the board (1/3 meter tall).
• Air write the letter (use a straight arm) and describe how to write the letter as 
you do it. Invite pupils to air write with you and say the sound. Watch them as 
they do it.
• Ask pupils to write the letter with a finger on their desks while saying the sound of 
the letter.
• Ask pupils to take out their exercise books and write the letter "m" 5 times.
• If some pupils finish early, tell them to draw a picture of something that begins 
with the sound /m/.

activities.title: Blend sounds
activities.content:
Tongue twister-blend sounds
• Recite the tongue twister from yesterday.  
Maamaa Maanee la maanoo be maloo 
bulu mandiinabaa
• Ask pupils what sound they hear most.
• Ask pupils what letter makes that sound.
• Say:  ''Saayiŋ n be kulukaŋo doolu fo la le. Ali ŋà kulukaŋolu coki ñoola I ye ì kafu 
kulu keelu kaŋ ǹ diyaamuta kumoolu mennu la.''
• Say the sounds /m/ /aa/. Ask pupils to blend the sounds together to make a 
syllable from the tongue twister. (Answer: maa).
• Repeat with the sounds /n/ /ee/. (Answer: /nee/).
• Say each syllable "maa"." "nee"
• Turn and talk: Ask pupils to turn to a pupil next to them and say the word made by 
those syllables.
• Call on 1-2 pupils to say what word is made when they blend the sounds and 
syllables together.

activities.title: Vocabulary – before reading
activities.content:
Teach and discuss vocabulary
• Tell pupils each word. Have them repeat it. Talk to the pupils about the new words 
they will hear in the text. Ask pupils what they know about each one.
• Discuss with students the word meaning, using gestures or illustrations to support 
understanding.  
Senelaa, Faloo, Mansatafil

activities.content:
Prediction based on title
• Say: ''N be naa taaliŋo karanna. N be taaliŋo too fo la le ye le. N lafit ali ye ì miira 
taaliŋo be kela muune ti. Taaliŋo too mu "Senelaa niŋ Faloo"
• Turn and Talk: Ask pupils to turn to a pupil next to them and make a guess 
(prediction) about the story.
• Call on 2 pupils at random and ask them for their predictions.

activities.title: Read aloud
activities.content:
Read the following story aloud
• Ask pupils to do a thumbs up if they hear one of the new vocabulary words during 
the read aloud.
• Show the picture that goes with the story as you read aloud. 
• While reading, pause to think aloud and talk to pupils about the story at key 
moments such as when you come to a vocabulary word the pupils just learnt or 
when you hear a syllable the pupils just practiced.
Senelaa niŋ Faloo
Senelaa doo le nene tarata Baaraa. Luŋ wo luŋ, a ka dookuwo ke baake a la kunkoo to. 
A ye ñamboolu tutu. Ñamboo ñiiñaata baake. Senelaa mu moo soonooyaariŋ baa le ti.
A ye ñamboo dii moo bee la-Mansa musoo baamaa aniŋ Mansa kee fanaŋ. Luŋ kiliŋ, 
Mansa kee ko, ''Ñamboo samba naŋ juurari lu¿o.'' Senelaa taata a la kunkoo to. Aniŋ 
faloo benta, Siloo kaŋ. Faloo ko I saama senelaa! Senelaa ko faloo ye I saama n baa 
diŋ.
Faloo ko,''dukaree n maakoyi ŋa minaŋo bayi. A be n na ñaamoo bee domo kaŋ ne'' 
Senelaa ko,''faloo ye niŋ I ye n samba, n be I maakoyi la le.'' Senelaa seleta faloo kaŋ ì 
niŋ boroo ì ye minaŋo bayi.
Bari minaŋo tariyaata baake boroo la le. Ì maŋ a muta noo. Wo koolaa leŋ senelaa ye 
a la kidoo taa buum! Minaŋo silanta baake a boroo ta dulaa jaŋ.
Faloo ko, '' n be I maakoyi la le ka ñamboo samba mansakee yaa.'' Moo bee kontaanita 
mansakee yaa. Mansakee ko, a baraka faloo, dukaree sabatiŋ ǹ fee jaŋ.'' Faloo 
sabatita ì fee jee a ka moolu maakoyi.

activities.title: Comprehension – Prediction check
activities.content:
Check predictions based on title
• Remind the class what the volunteer pupil predicted before the read aloud. Ask 

the pupils if his prediction was matched what was in the story.
• Ask the other pupils to think about what they predicted. Call on 2 pupils at 
random. Ask what they predicted, why, and if what they predicted is what 
happened in the story.
5. Vocabulary - after reading (5 mins)
Check for vocabulary understanding
• Ask pupils if they heard the new vocabulary words during the read aloud.
• Call on 3-4 pupils to say what vocabulary word they heard and to say the meaning 
in their own words.
• Say: '' Ali ŋà kumoolu taa ŋà mennu karaŋ ka ¥ munafaŋ ì la ka diyaamoo kutoolu 
dedaa.''
• Give an example by using one of the words in a new sentence - a sentence that is 
not in the pupil book or read aloud.
• For each other vocabulary word introduced before reading, ask a pupil to use the 
word in a new sentence. Have pupils act out a word, if appropriate. Congratulate, 
help, or correct the pupils, depending on the responses.
• Remind pupils that they can use these words anytime throughout the day. 
Encourage pupils to share the words with their families at home.

activities.content:

activities.title: Read syllables

Rapid syllable reading
• Write the first column of Box #3 on the board.

• Write each additional column, one at a time. Have pupils read the syllables in each 

column.
• Point to 5 syllables at random. Ask the whole class to read them quickly, as you

activities.title: Decodable story reading – In pairs
activities.content:
Pupils read in pairs

other read challenging words.
• Walk around the room while pupils read. Encourage pupils to use skills they have 
learnt to read words. They should blend sounds to read syllables, and blend

activities.title: Comprehension – making connections
activities.content:
Ask comprehension questions 
• Call on a pupil randomly to answer the following question:
• Question 1: Jaabi lee? [Answer: A be naakoo to]
• Question 2: Jaabi ye meŋ feŋ koteŋ ne soto ala naakoto? (Answer: A ye Jaato, 
kanjoo, kaanoo a la naakoo to)· 
• After each question, call on a pupil randomly to share their answer to the 
question. 
• Discuss their answers with the class. Help the pupils think about what is in the 
text or picture, as well as their own experiences, to reflect on what may have 
given them that idea.
Make text-to-self connections
• Say: Fo ali ye naakoo soto ali la suwoolu kono? Muŋ fii fext jumaalu le be je?
• Ask pupils to turn to a partner to share their answers.
• Call on a pupil randomly to share their answer to the question. Discuss their 
answer with the class. Help the pupils think about how the story relates to their 
own lives and how they can use their own experiences to understand the story.

activities.title: Writing – Story response
activities.content:
Pupils write or draw a response to the story
• Ask pupils to take out their exercise books.
• Ask pupils to draw or write about the text-to-self connection they made to the 
story.

activities.title: Letter and keyword
activities.content:
Teach the letter
• Point to the small letter "m" on the alphabet poster or on the board.
• Say: ''Ñiŋ ne mu ǹ na kulukutoo ti bii. Ñiŋ kuloo le ka /p/kulukaŋo fo. Ali ŋa fo 
ñoola.
• Ask pupils to say the sound with you (no more than 2 times).
• Point to the capital letter "M" on the alphabet poster or on the board.

• Say: Ñiŋ mu ate kulukiliŋo le ti. Ñiŋ kuloo le ka /m /kulukaŋo fo. Niŋ a naata 
diyaamoo datidulaa to waraŋ moo too, dulaa too n be a je la tenne.'
• Point to the small letter /m/ on the alphabet poster or on the board again.
• Say:  "Waati jamaa la, ¥ be a je la teŋ ne kumoolu kono."
Keyword picture study
• Say: Munne mu ñiŋ ti?
• Call on 1-2 pupils to name what they see in the picture.
• Say the keyword. Touch the letter of the day in the keyword in the pupil book. Say 
the sound. 
• Say: Ali ŋà kumoo fo ñoola: '/maanoo/.' Fo ali ye /m/ kuluka¿o moyi le maanoo 
kumoo kono"?
· Ask pupils to touch the letter and say the word again. 
Keyword analysis (Pupil Book Box #1)
• Write the keyword from Box #1 on the board. 
• Point to the keyword.
• Say: Kumoo mu "maanoo" le ti.
• Point to the syllable (under the keyword). Read it and show pupils how the syllable 
is part of the keyword.
• Point to the letter (under the syllable). Read it and show pupils how the letter is 
part of the syllable.

activities.title: Read syllables
activities.content:
Use the new letter sound to read syllables (Pupil Book Box #2)
• Write the Box #2 syllable column on the board.
• Point to the first syllable. Cover the "aa" and show the "m".
• Say: kulukaŋ jumaa le mu ñiŋ ti? (pupils respond "m")
• Cover the "m" and show the "aa" .
• Say: kulukaŋ jumaa le mu ñiŋ ti? (pupils respond "aa" ) .
• Say: '' Ali si kulukaŋolu karaŋ noo ñoola le wo koolaa ali ye ì coki ñoola ka 
kumabuloo dedaa. Saayiŋ kulukaŋolu karaŋ aniŋ ali ye ì coki ñoola:/m/ /aa/, 
'maa' ''
• Continue in this way for the other syllables. Ask pupils to do the others. They will 
say each sound, and then the syllable. 
• After the pupils have read all the syllables together, give them 1 minute to try 
reading the syllables independently again from their books.
Rapid syllable reading (Pupil Book Box #3)
• Write the first column of Box #3 on the board.

• Ask pupils, all together, to read down the column on the board. 
• Write each additional column, one at a time. Have pupils read the syllables in each 
column.
• Point to 5 syllables randomly. Ask the whole class to read each one quickly as you 
point to it.

activities.title: Read words
activities.content:
Blending syllables to read words
• Write the first word on the chalkboard and help pupils find it in their books.
• Say: Ali i lamoyi kuuke ali ye a juubee. N be kumabuloo karanna ŋa naa kulukaŋolu 
coki ñoola ka kumoo dedaa.''
• Model the blending process by reading each syllable, then blending the syllables 
together to read the word.
• Say: Ali ŋà a kata ñoola'.
• Read the same syllables and the word, but this time with the pupils. Then ask the 
pupils to try the same word by themselves.
• Say: Saayiŋ ali ye a loŋ ne ali ñanta meŋ kela. Wo sila kiliŋo ñaama, kumaa doolu 
karaŋ I la bukoo kono. Foloo, foloo, kumabuloo karaŋ wo koolaa i ye kumoo fo. 
Coodiroo ke i bulukondiŋo la i ye bula a nooma.''(Monitor and help pupils.)
• Call on 4 pupils at random to read one of the words using the blending process - 
reading the syllables, then the word. Provide help if needed.
